nodes.notes: Loop controller — releases 10 item(s) per pass. Output 2 (loop) processes the batch, output 1 (done) fires after the last batch. Watch out: Output 2 is the loop body, output 1 fires once after the last batch. Wiring these backwards is the classic mistake.

nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Lead Tracker', matched on leadId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per lead (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

# Nurture subscribers: Google Sheets & Discord

**Pattern:** Drip Sequence · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers outreach work end to end across Google Sheets, Discord and Google Drive.

It moves through 21 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets)
3. Normalize Lead Payload
4. Work in Batches
5. Process Batch Item
6. Respect Rate Limits
7. Aggregate Batch Results
8. Mark Completed in Google Sheets
9. Stamp Completion Time
10. Persist Run Metadata
11. Fingerprint for Idempotency
12. Drop Already-Processed Items
13. Load Previous Snapshot
14. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
15. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
16. Archive Copy to Google Drive
17. Enrich with Reference Data
18. Fold In Enrichment Fields
19. Summarize Run Stats
20. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
21. Send Summary to Discord

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing outreach work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets) → Normalize Lead Payload → Work in Batches → Process Batch Item → Respect Rate Limits → Aggregate Batch Results → Mark Completed in Google Sheets → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Copy to Google Drive → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Discord → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Discord aligned by hand for outreach
- Outreach sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Google Sheets
- A backlog too large to push into Google Sheets in one pass, across 24 nodes
- Outreach work where "Read Pending Queue (Google Sheets)" is still a manual step before Google Sheets

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Discord in step for outreach, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Discord are skipped, across all 24 nodes of this outreach build
- A failed Google Sheets or Discord call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 24 nodes in this outreach build
- The pause before Google Sheets is durable — a outreach run survives a restart
- Batches the work so Google Sheets rate limits never break a outreach run

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Discord webhook URL; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The batch size and the Wait between iterations exist specifically to respect the downstream API's rate limit — processing everything as fast as possible just gets the workflow throttled or banned. Marking items completed only after a batch succeeds leaves a clean resume point if the run dies mid-way, instead of an ambiguous half-processed state.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Lower the batch size and raise the wait — measure the throughput/reliability tradeoff directly.
2. Simulate a failed item mid-batch and see exactly what 'Mark Completed' captures.
3. Point the queue read at a different store platform.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**The loop runs forever or exits immediately**
Cause: The loop output and the done output are wired the wrong way round.
Fix: Output 2 is the loop body; output 1 fires after the last batch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your outreach process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
outreach payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
